an6.46:1.2: The Cetīs were a rather obscure people living in the Bundelkhand division of Madhya Pradesh, south of Vaccha and west of Magadha, around the Vettavatī river (Sanskrit _vetravatī_, modern Betwa), a tributary of the Yamunā flowing from the Vindhya ranges to the south. Two further discourses feature Mahācunda there ([an10.24](), [an10.85]()), and only one other ([sn56.30]()). A century after the Buddha, Revata stopped there heading south from Saṅkassa, where ten leading monks met him to discuss the dispute at the upcoming Second Council ([pli-tv-kd22:1.9.39]()). | The spelling of the city is highly uncertain: _sayaṁjāti_, _sahajāti_, _sañjāti_, _sahañcanika_, _sahajaniya_. The commentary to [ja422]() says the name of the Cetī capital was Sotthivatī, sometimes identified with Śuktimatī found in Sanskrit sources. Possibly these variants reflect attempts to render the local dialect. The sense of the name is “one’s own caste”, perhaps suggesting they were an insular people.
